subject.title: Slack thread replies can be generated but not delivered after origin tuple is lost

question: Is the July 1 sanitized incident evidence enough to authorize a source-level Slack delivery fix now, or should implementation wait for the reduced QA/live sequence described in the July 6 triage comment?
rationale: The code shows plausible partial gaps, but the missing transition proof determines whether the fix belongs at Slack send confirmation, final-delivery recovery, active-reply cleanup, or a shared durable-send layer.

options.title: Wait for reduced proof
options.body: Keep the issue open and require the reduced QA/live event sequence before authorizing a fix so the owner boundary is not guessed.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded source fix now
options.body: A maintainer may explicitly accept source-level risk and direct a narrow fix around Slack thread confirmation plus pending final-delivery recovery.

options.title: Close only with new contrary proof
options.body: Close only if a later live/current-main reproduction attempt proves generated finals already become confirmed or failed delivery states for this scenario.

recommendation.title: Wait for reduced proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require the reduced QA/live event sequence before authorizing a fix so the owner boundary is not guessed.
